intro.author: Not named. Jewish tradition in the Talmud credits Samuel. The repeated line 'in those days there was no king in Israel' suggests it was written or completed when Israel had kings.
intro.written: Uncertain; traditionally early in the monarchy (around 1000 BC), while many scholars date its final form to the 600s–500s BC
intro.audience: Israel in the time of the kings, looking back on the unsettled years before the monarchy
intro.setting: The book covers the long stretch between Joshua's death and the rise of Samuel and Saul. Israel's tribes lived scattered among Canaanites with no central government, worship drifted toward local gods, and neighboring peoples raided and ruled them. In each crisis God raised up a 'judge,' more a rescuer and tribal leader than a courtroom judge.
intro.purpose: To show the repeating cycle of unfaithfulness, oppression, crying out and rescue, and how badly Israel needed faithful leadership and a faithful heart.
intro.bigIdea: When God's people forget him, life unravels, yet God keeps raising up deliverers.

outline.title: An unfinished conquest and a downward cycle
Everyone did what was right in his own eyes
